title: The per-schema seed volumes, the seeding order across the 19 baselines and the cutover from the one recovery schema are not stated
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 8, 9, 20 and 41; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 065 Sandbox database with synthetic recovery data v1.md sections 3, 4, 11 and 13
description: RWB-E1-065 builds one database rwb_sandbox with schema public for the ACE test double and schema recovery for 92 tables, the four extension tables and the 30 views, seeded with 2,812 cases from seed 20261128. Architecture v5 gives 19 rwb_* schemas with one login each and the Ownership Map gives each table an owner, but no source states how the build resolves every one of the 92 tables to one of the 19 schemas, the order in which the 19 baselines are applied and seeded when foreign keys stay inside a schema, the seed volume per schema, or whether the sandbox remains one database. The generator reads sys_objects, sys_fields and lov_value, which are themselves owned by rwb-source-data and may not exist until the per-service DB stories have run. The integration run cannot assert the split sandbox without those values.
evidence: Legacy section 3 (one rwb_sandbox on PostgreSQL 17), section 4 steps 2 to 10 (schema public and schema recovery, V0001 to V0003, seed 20261128, 1,226 Mortgage, 1,296 Hire purchase, 290 SSME, 10 cases per shape), section 11 (all tables in schema recovery) and section 13 (properties and eight build steps); Arch v5 slides 8 and 9 (one ACE PostgreSQL, 30 recovery.v_ace_* views, 19 rwb_* schemas, one login each), slide 20 (every service owns its schema with outbox and inbox) and slide 41 (one row per service with schema and wave); Ownership Map v1 table owners.
proposed: Keep one rwb_sandbox database, schema public for the ACE test double, schema recovery for the 30 views and helper functions, and one rwb_* schema per service; apply the 19 baselines in the wave order of Arch v5 slide 41 and seed a schema only after its own baseline; keep seed 20261128 and 2,812 cases as the total and split it by the table owner in the Ownership Map; publish the per-schema counts in the build report until a source fixes them.

title: The cross-service ledger-write contract and its failure mapping are not defined
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 066 Interaction ledger store and writer v1.md sections 3, 4, 12 and 13; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json api and table interaction; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 11, 15 and 41
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 13 Solution plan
description: In RWB-E1-066 the ledger is written by InteractionLedgerWriter.append() with Propagation.MANDATORY inside the P3 handler's transaction, so the action and the entry commit or roll back together. Under the R-PREC default ruling and DP-18 the ledger belongs to rwb-source-data, and the Ownership Map gives POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions and GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions to P1. No source states the request and response fields of that remote command, the Idempotency-Key rule, the status and message returned when P1 cannot write (the legacy 503 with MSG-P1-022), how a caller avoids committing an action without its entry once the call crosses a service boundary, or how a retry returns the first entry. The harness can assert the outcomes but cannot fix the wire contract.
evidence: Legacy section 3 (the caller holds Case record C and calls append()), section 4 steps 2 to 8 (same transaction, advisory lock, 201 with the Interaction), section 12 (published interface InteractionLedgerWriter.append and the P3 endpoint POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions) and section 13 (Propagation.MANDATORY, MSG-P1-022 on failure); Ownership Map v1 api POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions owner P1 and table interaction owner P1; Arch v5 slide 11 (Idempotency-Key on every POST, 2 s timeout, one hop) and slide 15 (P1 IN: /customers/{id}, /accounts/{id}, /freshness); Template and Rules section R3 default ruling (interaction ledger to P1) and DP-18.
proposed: Publish the append as POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions with an Idempotency-Key; P1 writes the entry, its local decision record and its outbox row in one transaction in rwb_source_data and answers 201 with the entry ID and case_seq, 200 or 409 with the first entry on a repeated key, 422 MSG-GEN-001 on an invalid field and 503 MSG-P1-022 when the write fails; the caller is a saga step that treats any non-2xx as a failed action and never keeps an action without its entry.

title: The event-to-ledger map, the cross-topic ordering rule and the duplicate key after the split into per-service topics are not defined
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 067 Every Workbench action into the interaction ledger v1.md sections 3, 4, 8 and 12; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 11, 14, 16, 42 and 43; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json events EV-01, EV-02, EV-04, EV-08, EV-16 and EV-19
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria; 12.4 Events consumed; 13 Solution plan
description: RWB-E1-067 maps six events from one outbox to six ledger event codes and dedupes on one idempotency key. In the target the six events are produced by three services on three topics: CaseCreated, CaseAllocated, CaseTransferred and TimerBreached on rwb.case.events.v1, DocumentStored on rwb.document.events.v1, and DecisionRecorded on the shared rwb.decision-record.v1. No source states the CloudEvents types and schema versions P1 subscribes to after the split, whether P1 runs one consumer group across the three topics, how per-case order is kept when Kafka orders only within a partition of one topic, how the R-UNI-40 hit count is kept when one action can appear on two topics, or which event version P1 accepts. The run cannot assert exactly-one-entry and order without those rules.
evidence: Legacy section 3 (RWB-TE-006 outbox, six events and the listener identity), section 4 steps 1 to 9 (one outbox, one listener, configured map, duplicate service, retry then exception queue), section 8 BR1 to BR7 (map, order per case, current and previous schema version, R-UNI-40) and section 12 (listener input and idempotency key); Arch v5 slides 14, 16, 42 and 43 (event catalogue: six events and three topics), slide 11 (CloudEvents binary mode, key caseId, retry 1 min/10 min/1 h then .dlt, inbox dedupe); Ownership Map v1 events EV-01, EV-02, EV-04, EV-08, EV-16 and EV-19.
proposed: P1 runs one consumer group across the three topics, accepts the current and previous schema version of each event, dedupes on the CloudEvents id in rwb_source_data.processed_event with the event idempotency key as the business key, and assigns case_seq under the case lock at append; the ledger read orders by occurredAt and then case_seq, and the run reports a cross-topic inversion that occurredAt cannot resolve instead of silently reordering. The event-to-code map stays the legacy map (EV-01 CASE_CREATED, EV-02 CASE_ALLOCATED, EV-04 CASE_TRANSFERRED, EV-08 DECISION_TAKEN, EV-16 DOCUMENT_ATTACHED, EV-19 CASE_ESCALATED).

title: The 19 login names, the grant matrix on the 30 ACE views and the two-part boundary rule after the schema split are not stated
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 069 Read only ACE source views, grants and boundary rule v1.md sections 3, 4, 12 and 13; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 8, 9, 11 and 41; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json extension tables
description: RWB-E1-069 fixes two roles (ace_view_owner and recovery_svc), one recovery schema and boundary rule BND-6 over recovery.v_ace_*. Architecture v5 gives 19 rwb_* schemas with one login each, and only rwb-source-data may read the 30 views. No source names the 19 logins, states whether each of the other 18 logins is denied on public and on the views, says whether the views stay owned by one role in schema recovery, or defines how BND-6 and the conformance test change when the 92 tables and the four extension tables sit in 19 schemas and the views stay in one. The integration run cannot assert the grant matrix without that list.
evidence: Legacy section 3 (ace_view_owner, recovery_svc), section 4 steps 1 to 8 (V0002, V0003, conformance test, BND-6), section 12 (grant block and grantees) and section 13 (components and build steps); Arch v5 slides 8 and 9 (ACE schemas + 30 recovery.v_ace_* views + 19 rwb_* schemas, one login each), slide 11 (SQL view: one login rwb_source_data, 5 s statement timeout) and slide 41 (19 schemas and logins); Ownership Map v1 extension tables party_ext, contact_point_ext, account_ext and valuation_ext owner P1; Environment and Deployment Design is not in the source set.
proposed: Keep the 30 views in schema recovery owned by ace_view_owner; give rwb_source_data SELECT on the views and no privilege in public; give each of the other 18 service logins no privilege on public or on the views; keep PUBLIC with nothing; and make BND-6 two build rules, no class names public and no class outside rwb-source-data names a v_ace_* view or another service's schema, with the allowed list read from the module map. Take the 19 login names from Environment and Deployment Design when it is issued.

title: The worker registration, task-queue and namespace contract between the 19 services and the Temporal platform is not defined
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 070 Temporal platform on the ACE AKS clusters v1.md sections 3, 4, 12 and 13; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 8, 9, 11, 23, 24 and 41; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md slides 7 and 8
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria; 12.5 Workflows and activities; 13 Solution plan
description: RWB-E1-070 builds one cluster, two persistence databases, the namespace rwb-recovery with 30-day retention and four search attributes, mTLS and an OIDC Web UI. Architecture v5 adds service workers, one task queue rwb-<short> per service in the same namespace, and a gateway route for staff screens. No source states the workload identity and client certificate each service uses, how a worker is registered and versioned per service, whether the queue list is fixed at platform install or created by the first worker, which codec key each service uses, the call shape of a cross-service step in the proof, or where the suite stores its evidence. The run cannot assert that each service polls only its own queue without that contract.
evidence: Legacy section 3 (approved version, certificates, ingress), section 4 steps 1 to 9 (Helm release, schema job, namespace job, mTLS, OIDC, metrics, run book, restart), section 12 (frontend gRPC, Web UI, metrics and health) and section 13 (Helm values, the two databases, the namespace and its settings); Arch v5 slides 8 and 9 (services, namespace rwb-recovery, task queue per service), slide 11 (Temporal: queue rwb-<svc>, contract jar, worker identity per service), slides 23 and 24 (one task queue per service, workers poll only their own queue) and slide 41 (19 queues); Temporal and Drools design slides 7 and 8 (L1 to L5, namespace and queue); Ownership Map v1 PlatformSmokeWorkflow owner PLT and JOB-22.
proposed: Register one worker per service on queue rwb-<short> in namespace rwb-recovery, with its own workload identity and a client certificate whose subject names the service; create the queues at platform install from the service catalogue and refuse a worker that polls a queue other than its own; give each service its own codec key under the namespace key; start the smoke workflow through RWB-PLT-E1070-APP on one named service queue; keep the 06:00 JOB-22 platform run out of this story; record the SIT evidence beside the run report and take the grant evidence from the rwb-access access review.
